The Soldier in Later Medieval England: A searchable database of muster rolls and garrison soldiery of (inter alia) The Hundred Years War and Henry V's 1415 campaign.

Reading Juliet Barker's magisterial Agincourt whilst tinkering around with some family history led me to wonder if Henry V's legendary record keeping had translated into anything that may be now digitised. Luckily, muster rolls for overseas expeditions (including garrisoning ports) have been transcribed and are searchable. If you'd like to learn a bit more about the men who fought in Agincourt, or sailed for France in one of the many episodes of the 100 years war, this database is fascinating.

Note: as with many databases, asterix acts as a wildcard. So if you are searching for a surname that starts Car (as in Carfax, Carmichael, Cartwright, etc) and you want to make sure your search caters for the innaccuracies of the muster role authors (and the usual fluidity of medieval surnames) then use the asterix. Example: Car*
